paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance of random example selection and the proposed STES at varying numbers of in-context examples.
model_annotation: The line chart compares the performance of two example selection methods—ST-ES (blue line with circular markers) and Random (orange line with circular markers)—as a function of the number of in-context examples, ranging from 0 to 8, with tick labels at integer intervals. The y-axis represents minADE₂₀ in units of meters (m), scaled linearly from 15.5 to 18.0, with major gridlines and tick labels at 0.5-unit intervals. The x-axis is labeled “Number of Examples” and uses a linear scale. The ST-ES line begins at a value of 17.0 at 0 examples, decreases to 15.5 at 2 examples, and then fluctuates slightly around 15.4–15.5 until 8 examples, where it ends at 15.4. The Random line begins at 18.0 at 0 examples, decreases to 17.2 at 2 examples, and then remains relatively flat around 17.0–17.1 until 8 examples, where it ends at 16.9.

model_annotations.English: This line plot compares the performance of two example selection strategies—ST-ES and Random—as measured by minADE₂₀ (in units of meters, as indicated by the label “minADE₂₀ (←)”) across varying numbers of in-context examples, which are plotted on the x-axis ranging from 0 to 8. The x-axis is labeled “Number of Examples” and uses a linear scale with tick marks at integer intervals from 0 to 8. The y-axis, labeled “minADE₂₀ (←)”, also uses a linear scale and ranges from approximately 15.4 to 18.0. The ST-ES strategy is represented by a blue line with circular markers and a solid line; it starts at a value of 17.0 when the number of examples is 0, declines sharply to approximately 15.45 at 2 examples, and then remains relatively flat, fluctuating slightly between approximately 15.4 and 15.5 until 8 examples. The Random strategy is represented by an orange line with circular markers and a solid line; it begins at a value of 18.0 when the number of examples is 0, and then gradually decreases to approximately 16.9 at 8 examples, leveling off around 16.95 between 4 and 8 examples.
